title: Introduce invocation-staleness metric and alert-prioritizer
author: David Nguyen
release_notes: Adds Invocation Staleness metric and alert prioritizer service; new Staleness Explorer dashboard; feature-flagged rollout with canary; non-breaking; docs and tests included.
description: Motivation: production customers have reported long idle gaps in streaming responses and silent delays between invocations that are not visible in existing token/latency telemetry. This PR introduces an "invocation_staleness" signal that captures idle windows (time from last emitted token to next invocation start and intra-invocation idle spikes) and wires it into observability, tracing, dashboarding, and alert prioritization. Changes include: server-side metric (histogram + summary) for staleness, trace enrichment with last_active timestamps and staleness tags, a lightweight Alert Prioritizer service that ranks alerts by estimated customer cost, affected tenant SLA tier, and signal confidence, a Staleness Explorer dashboard for root-cause investigation, and a feature flag (obs.staleness.enabled) for staged rollout. Checklist: [x] metric collection and aggregation; [x] trace span enrichment; [x] alert prioritizer implementation; [x] console dashboard; [x] unit and integration tests; [x] docs and runbook; [x] gated rollout plan. Testing: unit tests for metric computation, integration tests exercising tracing enrichment against a local trace collector, canary enabled on 5% of traffic in prod region eu-west-1 with e2e synthetic invocations. CI: one flaky integration test required a rerun but passed on second attempt. Rollout plan: enable feature-flag in canary for 72h, monitor SLO regressions and alert noise, increase to 25% then full rollout after 7 days if no regressions. Rollback: flip obs.staleness.enabled off to stop enrichment and prioritizer scoring; metric data will remain but dashboard will show gaps. Risks & mitigations: minor extra tag cardinality from last_active keys (mitigated by coarse-bucketing and server-side rollups), potential alert churn from new staleness-driven alerts (mitigated by initial prioritizer quiet period and tuned thresholds). Related: complements ENG-1987 (token-level cost reconciler) and ENG-2040 (alert-suppression heuristics).
commits_summary: 1) add invocation staleness metric and aggregation pipeline; 2) trace enricher to attach last_active/staleness tags; 3) implement alert prioritizer service and config; 4) add Staleness Explorer dashboard JSON and console widgets; 5) feature-flag gating and small migration script; 6) tests and docs.
summary_changes: Server: new staleness metric and aggregation; Tracing: enrich spans with last_active & staleness tag; Alerting: new prioritizer service that scores alerts by cost/impact/confidence; Console: Staleness Explorer dashboard and drilldowns; Telemetry pipeline: coarse bucketing to control cardinality; Feature flag for rollout; Tests and docs added.
review_conversation: Asha: Can you justify the added cardinality for last_active tag? David: We bucket last_active into 1s/5s/30s/1m/5m buckets upstream and only emit the bucket tag, not raw timestamps, to limit cardinality. Marco: Prioritizer needs a safety cutoff to avoid demoting critical alerts; David: added rule to force-promote alerts with error-rate > 5% or SLA impact flag. Lena: Integration test failed on CI the first run; David: reran CI, fixed a race in the test harness and added a deterministic timeout, all tests now pass. Asha: suggest adding a small rate limiter on enrichment to avoid amplification during bursts; David: added a token-bucket limiter in staleness_span_enricher and tested under load. Approvals: Asha approved 2026-02-20; Marco approved after minor config tweak 2026-02-21; Lena approved 2026-02-22. Merge: squash.
